verdict: Avoid new wholesale-trade exposure in Kolkata for now; lend only to named, cash-and-carry distributors with clean stock statements and no cash-handling exposure, and treat Barabazar-style cash/credit intermediaries as off-limits.
title: Kolkata Wholesale Trade: a note to the credit manager
narrative: The working-capital cycle is the whole business: inventory days plus receivable days minus payable days. Capex is light (godown, racks, a delivery vehicle), so the loan is almost always for stock and receivables, not assets. **So when a proposal lands, check the receivable days against the payable days first; if receivables stretch beyond payables, ask what the trader is funding and from where.**

## What has changed now
**The local demand signal is negative: West Bengal GST collections are -1.3% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, and electricity demand is +5.7% against India +9.5% [D].** That is a state-level stress read, not a Kolkata-specific one — the sources say little about the city itself, so lean on first principles and peers. Nationally, bank credit is running +29.1% YoY against activity of +6.1% [D], and the repo is 5.5% with a tightening stance [D]; **so the system is lending faster than the real economy is growing, which means weaker traders are being kept alive on fresh credit — check whether your borrower's sales growth is real or refinanced.** Locally, a cash-fraud gang has been targeting Barabazar traders with fake currency bundles [2], and the drug control department raided the wholesale medicine market at Mehta Building [3]. Commercial LPG rose by Rs 10 a cylinder ahead of Kali Puja [1] — a direct cost hit for food and hospitality wholesalers.

## Where the growth is
**Peer results point to wholesale as a live channel: Aditya Birla Lifestyle's wholesale channel grew 18% in Q2FY27 [7], and Tata Motors' commercial-vehicle demand is strong [4].** For Kolkata, pursue organised distributors of FMCG, lifestyle and auto spares who sell to a documented retailer base and can show GST-matched invoices. **Avoid the cash-and-carry intermediaries in Barabazar and the medicine wholesale cluster until the fraud and raid issues settle [2][3].** Mishka Exim, a listed trader, shows 234.87% sales growth but gross margin of only 11.5% and ROE of 8.5% [5] — **so when a fast-growing trader applies, check the gross margin; if it is below 12%, ask how the loan is serviced from such thin spreads.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure as a cash-credit or bill-discounting limit against GST-matched invoices, not a term loan.** Take stock and receivable statements every month, GST returns every month, and a physical godown check quarterly. Covenant on receivable days and on the share of sales to the top five buyers.
